title.narrative: Outcome 1: Timely and quality health care is provided to conflict-affected and vulnerable populations.

Indicator 1: Number of people provided with health care services by the end of the programme (disaggregated by sex and gender). Target: Syria: 92.000, Lebanon: 565.
Indicator 2: Number of people provided with sanitation items and information on how to prevent covid-19 (disaggregated by sex and gender). Target: Syria: 92.000.
Indicator 3: Number of staff and volunteers trained on health topics (disaggregated by sex, age, and training topic). Target: Syria: 40
Indicator 4: Percentage of programme health beneficiaries who also received PSS services. Target: Syria: 5%, Lebanon: 10%.
Outcome 2: Timely and relevant psychosocial support is delivered to vulnerable individuals and communities by well.capacitated RCRC National Societies.

Indicator 1: Number of people reached with basic and focused psychosocial support by the end of the programme (disaggregated by sex, age, and psychosocial support service). Target: Syria: 32.278, Lebanon: 4500, Iraq: 3000.
Indicator 2: Number of staff and volunteers trained on psychosocial support approaches and/or protection mainstreaming (disaggregated by sex, age, training topic, and National Societies). Target: Syria: 240, Lebanon: 150, Iraq: 20.
Indicator 3: Percentage of staff and volunteers who report improved knowledge of psychosocial support approaches and/or protection mainstreaming. Target: Syria: 80%, Lebanon: LRC 80% and PRCS-L 80%, Iraq: 80%.
Indicator 4: Number of at risk and out-of-school children and youth who received non-formal education (remedial classes, homework clubs, literacy classes) disaggregated by sex, age, and class type. Target: Syria: 800.
Outcome 3: Timely and relevant basic relief assistance is delivered to vulnerable individuals and communities by well-capacitated RCRC National Societies.

Indicator 1: Number of people reached with basic relief by the end of the programme (disaggregated by sex, age, and disability). Target: Syria: 15.790, Lebanon: 1740, Iraq: 1895.
Indicator 2: Number of staff and volunteers trained on CVA/relief topics (disaggregated by sex, age, training topic and NS). Target: Syria: 80, Lebanon: 35, Iraq: 25.
Indicator 3: Percentage of staff and volunteers who demonstrate improved cash preparedness and knowledge of cash/relief distribution programming. Target: Syria: 70%, Lebanon: 85%
Outcome 4: Improved employability skills and livelihood opportunities are provided to vulnerable individuals.

Indicator 1: Number of vulnerable individuals who received vocational training and cash/in kind support for social/economic inclusion (disaggregated by sex, age, disability and training topic). Target: Syria: 120.
Indicator 2: Percentage of vocational training beneficiaries who report an increase in skills, motivation, and confidence to apply got a job, start a business or start an education. Target: Syria: 75%.
Output 2.1: People are reached with basic and focused psychosocial support by the end of the programme
Indicator 1: Number of people reached with basic and focused psychosocial support by the end of the programme (disaggregated by sex, age, and psychosocial support service).
Output 2.3: Staff and volunteers report improved knowledge of psychosocial support approaches and/or protection mainstreaming
Indicator 3: Percentage of staff and volunteers who report improved knowledge of psychosocial support approaches and/or protection mainstreaming.

target.value: Syria: 80% Lebanon: LRC: 80% ad PRCS-L 80% Iraq: 80%

actual.value:
Syria: 109.445 (target: 32.278). More than three times as many beneficiaries as the target were reached because the PSS outreach teams were able to expand their services in additional geographical areas and additional categories such as remedial classes, COVID-19 awareness, caregiver sessions, risk reduction, and protection awareness.
Lebanon: 4924 (target: 4500).
Iraq: 7674 (target: 3000)

title.narrative: Output 3.1: People are reached with basic relief by the end of the programme (disaggregated by sex, age, and disability)
Indicator 1: Number of people reached with basic relief by the end of the programme (disaggregated by sex, age, and disability).

actual.value:
Syria: 14.345 (target: 15.790) beneficiaries were provided with basic relief.
Lebanon: 1657 (target: 1740) beneficiaries were provided with basic relief.
Iraq: 2175 (target: 1895) beneficiaries were provided with basic relief.

title.narrative: Output 4.1: Vulnerable individuals received vocational training and cash/in kind support for social/economic inclusion (disaggregated by sex, age, disability and training topic)
Indicator 1: Number of vulnerable individuals who received vocational training and cash/in kind support for social/economic inclusion (disaggregated by sex, age, disability and training topic).

actual.value: Syria: 140 (target: 120) vulnerable individuals received vocational training and cash/in kind support for social/economic inclusion.

title.narrative: Output 2.2: Staff and volunteers are trained on psychosocial support approaches and/or protection mainstreaming
Indicator 2: Number of staff and volunteers trained on psychosocial support approaches and/or protection mainstreaming (disaggregated by sex, age, training topic, and National Societies).

actual.value:
Syria: 289 (target: 240)
Lebanon: 365 (target: 150) staff and volunteers received training on psychosocial support approaches and/or protection mainstreaming. The reason for this high achievement was because LRC conducted more trainings as a result of contracting two experienced consultants to dedicate their time to rolling out training, as well as due to training being online because of COVID-19 restrictions which led to more participants.
Iraq: 55 (target 20)

title.narrative: Output 2.4: At risk and out-of-school children and youth received non-formal education (remedial classes, homework clubs, literacy classes) disaggregated by sex, age, and class type
Indicator 4: Number of at risk and out-of-school children and youth who received non-formal education (remedial classes, homework clubs, literacy classes) disaggregated by sex, age, and class type.

actual.value: Syria: 529 (target: 800) at-risk and out-of-school children and youth received non-formal education. Due to COVID-19 restrictions, the size of classes was smaller than planned.

title.narrative: Output 1.1: People are provided with health care services
Indicator 1: Number of people provided with health care services by the end of the programme (disaggregated by sex and gender).

actual.value:
Syria: 53.315 (target: 92.000) beneficiaries were provided with health care services. The number of people provided with health care services slightly decreased compared to 2019 (63,256) and 2020 (57,362). However, the project set the target in 2021 to 92,000 beneficiaries and this was inaccurately done by relying on the number of consultations per day per clinic (averaged to 120 consultations per day) instead of actual beneficiary numbers. This led to the project achieving 58% of its target in 2021 even though the numbers reached between 2020 and 2021 only changed by 7%.
Lebanon: 1651 (target 565) beneficiaries were provided with health care services.

title.narrative: Output 1.4: Programme health beneficiaries are also receiving PSS services
Indicator 4: Percentage of programme health beneficiaries who also received PSS services.

actual.value:
Syria: 6,5% (target: 5%) of the health beneficiaries also received PSS services.
Lebanon: 4,2% (target: 10%) of the health beneficiaries also received PSS services. The reasons for the underachievement of this target were that the social workers had other competing tasks and so little time was dedicated to the PSS services, as well as this being a new activity for PRCS-L.

title.narrative: Output 4.2: Vocational training beneficiaries report an increase in skills, motivation, and confidence to apply for a job, start a business or start an education
Indicator 2: Percentage of vocational training beneficiaries who report an increase in skills, motivation, and confidence to apply for a job, start a business or start an education.

actual.value: Syria: 83% of the participants (target: 75%) reported an increase in skills, motivation and confidence to apply for a job, start a business or start an education. 7 trainings were held with an average of 20 participants.

title.narrative: Output 1.3: Staff and volunteers are trained on health topics
Indicator 3: Number of staff and volunteers trained on health topics (disaggregated by sex, age, and training topic)

actual.value: Syria: 91 (target: 40) staff and volunteers were trained on health topics such as covid-19, diabetes, HIS/PJIS and medical waste management.

title.narrative: Output 1.2: People are provided with sanitation items and information on how to prevent covid-19
Indicator 2: Number of people provided with sanitation items and information on how to prevent covid-19 (disaggregated by sex and gender)

actual.value: Syria: : 53.315 (target: 92.000) beneficiaries were provided with sanitation items and information on covid-19 prevention

title.narrative: Output 3.3: Staff and volunteers demonstrate improved cash preparedness and knowledge of cash/relief distribution programming
Indicator 3: Percentage of staff and volunteers who demonstrate improved cash preparedness and knowledge of cash/relief distribution programming.

actual.value:
Syria: Output not achieved due to output 3.2 not being achieved.
Lebanon: 79% (target: 85%) of staff and volunteers demonstrated improved cash preparedness and knowledge of cash/relief distribution programming.

title.narrative: Output 3.2: Staff and volunteers are trained on CVA/relief topics (disaggregated by sex, age, training topic and NS)
Indicator 2: Number of staff and volunteers trained on CVA/relief topics (disaggregated by sex, age, training topic and NS).

actual.value:
Syria: Training of staff on CVA topics was not done because of challenges of transfers of funds from Denmark to Syria. DRC and the implementing partner had to prioritize activities with the cash in-country available, resulting in the cancellation of some activities such as the CVA training. Instead, an agreement was reached with SARC and British Red Cross that some of the trainings would be funded by the BRC, while the DRC would support the rest in 2022.
Lebanon: 17 (target: 35) LRC and PRCS-L staff and volunteers were trained on CVA/relief topics. Due to COVID-19, LRC conducted fewer trainings than anticipated.
Iraq: 21 (target: 25) IRCS staff and volunteers were trained on CVA/relief topics.
